1.note: Literally "when my glory was shaken out" (compare Neh 5:13 נָעוּר). It may mean that his honor was roused, that is, when he set out. Uncertain.

2.note: Gen 38:1, of the patriarch Judah. Here it points to the author, Judah al-Ḥarizi, who left Spain for the East.

3.note: Kaminka prints "river" in parentheses. Ahava is the river where Ezra gathered the exiles (Ezra 8:15, 21); the author identifies it with this place.

4.note: The print can also be read בפי. Read כפי, "about". A parasang is a Persian measure of distance.

5.note: It is not clear who prepared the place: the people or God.

6.he: יאמרו כי הארץ ההיא האל כל שוכניה הברית
6.note: Kaminka prints האל, which does not make sense here. Translated as if the text said that the dwellers broke (הפרו) the covenant (compare Isa 24:5), like Sodom; the next line (Isa 34:9) speaks of pitch and brimstone.

7.note: Gen 20:16 "a covering of the eyes". Here it seems to say that the sun borrowed its light from the light over the grave. Uncertain.

8.note: The print has הלב, "the heart". The line is unclear; perhaps a misprint.

9.note: The print looks like בכם; in this print ס and ם are hard to tell apart. Read כס יה, "the throne of Yah" (Exod 17:16).

10.note: Deut 34:7, said of Moses: "his vigor had not fled". The print looks like נם; read נס. Here it means that his body did not decay.

11.note: The words in brackets are added by Kaminka to complete the line. Ezek 1:10: the faces of a man and a lion on the right, an ox on the left, and an eagle.
